subject.title: fix(exec-approvals): handle same-process sync/async lock contention

question: During same-process policy mutation, must synchronous exec authorization wait or fail closed until the new policy commits, or may it use the previously committed policy?
rationale: The PR trades availability for a temporary stale-policy authorization window, and the permanent ordering contract for exec-policy revocation requires explicit security-owner intent.

options.title: Preserve revocation ordering
options.body: Keep synchronous authorization from using the old policy during an active writer and redesign the process-local coordination so reads consume only the writer's committed result or fail closed.

options.title: Allow stale committed reads
options.body: Accept that an exec may be authorized under the previous policy during the bounded same-process update window and document and test that contract.

options.title: Pause this approach
options.body: Leave the current fail-closed behavior in place until a design can fix the availability regression without weakening revocation ordering.

recommendation.title: Preserve revocation ordering
recommendation.body: Keep synchronous authorization from using the old policy during an active writer and redesign the process-local coordination so reads consume only the writer's committed result or fail closed.

likelyOwner.reason: The commit history most strongly connects this person to the exec-approval security model and central implementation.
